correctness.rationale: The three-torus parametrization gives exact Fourier orthogonality of every axis monomial against all other monomials, and the arcsine moment formula gives its norm for each nonnegative integer. The quotient RKHS and generating-series identity follow. Positive Taylor coefficients of \((1-t)^{3/2}S(t)\) have total nonconstant mass \(\pi/2-1<1\), proving a disk-wide nonzero bound. The negative quadratic coefficient of \(1-1/S(t)\) forbids the normalized complete-Pick condition, and restriction heredity extends the obstruction to the ambient kernel. Explicit first- and second-derivative estimates establish the sharp metric exponent. Independently executed CHECK.py passed 734 exact and high-precision assertions; none of the infinite results is inferred from a finite test.

Those explicit structural properties form the new claim. The classical reciprocal-binomial series and normalized Pick necessity are not claimed as original. Pal--Tomar study an admissible-kernel corona theorem instead; Alpay--Jorgensen study a different discrete binomial RKHS. The verified local and published-result comparisons showed no dominating exact pentablock claim. Independent global priority assessment remains outstanding.

value.rationale: The geometrically canonical axis of the recently introduced pentablock Hardy space has a precise, nonobvious arcsine radial quotient model, explicit evaluation kernel and sharp noninteger boundary singularity. A quantitative zero-free property of this restriction coexists with failure of complete Pick interpolation of the full space, a structural distinction relevant to operator interpolation on the new domain. The object is motivated before calculation by the unique first-coordinate fibre of the boundary map; it is not an arbitrary numerical slice, a copied generating-series identity or a claim about unrelated parameters.
